svg.title: Footprint pair aggregation uses existential visibility
svg.desc: Two two-cell footprints create four source-target sample pairs. Three red dashed paths are blocked and one blue path survives, so visible samples equals one of four and the aggregate result is visible.
svg.text: FOOTPRINTS / any visible pair exposes the target

rect.title: Origin footprint sample o₀: the first absolute source cell formed by adding the first footprint offset to the origin anchor.
Origin footprint sample o₁: the second absolute source cell; it supplies the only transparent pair in this example.
Target footprint sample t₀: the first absolute target cell; pair o₁→t₀ survives all blockers.
Target footprint sample t₁: the second target cell; both paths ending here are blocked in this example.

path.title: Pair o₀→t₀: blocked; it contributes zero to visibleSampleCount.
Pair o₀→t₁: blocked; existential aggregation does not require this path to pass.
Pair o₁→t₁: blocked; three failed pairs still leave the aggregate visible when one pair succeeds.
Pair o₁→t₀: transparent through terrain and sampled boundaries; this single success makes visibleSamples greater than zero.

rect.title: Aggregate result: one of four pairs is visible, so visibleSamples = 1, totalSamples = 4, and visible = true.

g.text: The visibility evaluator retains the exact count 1/4; downstream combat may later interpret visible and total samples as a trace ratio.1 / 4

svg.text: This is exposure, not unanimity: one unobstructed footprint pair is sufficient.
